source_name: CBCG — Regulativa (regulatory framework hub, ME)
why_relevant: Top-level hub of the CBCG legal corpus, branching into Ustav, Zakoni, Statut and Podzakonski akti. Single best entry point to enumerate every legally binding instrument the regulator issues or applies.

source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti (bylaws / Odluke, all categories)
why_relevant: The operative body of CBCG secondary legislation, organised into seven tracked categories: monetarni instrumenti, finansijska stabilnost, kontrola banaka, kontrola pruzalaca finansijskih usluga, zastita korisnika potrosackih kredita, platni promet i platni sistemi, sanacija kreditnih institucija. Each Odluka carries its Sluzbeni list citation, which gives an exact promulgation date and therefore a compliance-deadline anchor.

source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti: Kontrola banaka (bank supervision bylaws)
why_relevant: Densest prudential sub-corpus: capital adequacy, minimum risk-management standards, key-function/business-line criteria, reporting content and deadlines, AML/CFT risk-system guidelines. Observed instruments include Odluka o minimalnim standardima za upravljanje rizicima u kreditnim institucijama (Sl. list CG 134/21) and Odluka o sadrzaju, rokovima i nacinu sacinjavanja i dostavljanja finansijskih izvjestaja banaka (34/22) — the latter is literally a deadline schedule.

source_name: CBCG — Regulations (English mirror of the bylaw corpus)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the same seven regulation categories (Monetary Instruments, Financial Stability, Banking Supervision, Resolution of Credit Institutions, Supervision of Financial Service Providers, Protection of Consumer Loan Beneficiaries, Payment Operations and Payment Systems). Useful for cross-lingual term alignment and for consumers who cannot read Montenegrin, but is typically less complete/lagging versus the ME tree — always reconcile against ME.

source_name: CBCG — Zakoni (laws administered/drafted by the central bank)
why_relevant: Consolidated set of the primary statutes the CBCG applies — Zakon o Centralnoj banci, Zakon o kreditnim institucijama, Zakon o platnom prometu, Zakon o sanaciji kreditnih institucija, Zakon o sprjecavanju pranja novca. Statutory change is the upstream driver of every downstream Odluka and compliance deadline.

source_name: CBCG — Saopstenja (press releases, incl. Savjet CBCG session outcomes)
why_relevant: The earliest public signal for regulatory change: the Savjet CBCG (Council) adopts drafts and decisions at numbered sessions and each is announced here, typically weeks before Sluzbeni list publication. Observed examples: 'Savjet CBCG utvrdio nacrte zakona i odluke ... jacanja efikasnosti platnog sistema' and countercyclical buffer raised to 1% applicable from 1 January 2026 — a dated compliance deadline surfaced only via a press release.

source_name: CBCG — Kontrolna funkcija (supervisory function hub)
why_relevant: Hub for the supervisory perimeter: bankarski sistem, registar banaka, banks in bankruptcy, financial reports of banks, supervised non-bank providers (leasing, faktoring, otkup potrazivanja, mikrokreditne finansijske institucije, kreditno-garantni fond), recognised rating agencies, restriktivne mjere, AQR, and cooperation agreements. Defines who is licensed and therefore who is in scope for every deadline.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (register of licensed banks)
why_relevant: Authoritative licensing register for credit institutions. Diffs against it are the cleanest evidence of licence grants, withdrawals, mergers and market entry/exit.

source_name: CBCG — Registri platnog prometa (payment systems / payment institutions / e-money institutions)
why_relevant: Statutory registers maintained under the Zakon o platnom prometu: registar platnih sistema, registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata, registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata, plus the list of institutions whose authorisation was revoked. This is the licensing ground truth for the payments sector and directly serves the payments half of the run scope.

source_name: CBCG — Platni promet (payment system function hub)
why_relevant: Operational hub for the national payment system: RTGS and DNS systems, instant payments (TIPS clone), CBCG tariff, payment-institution/e-money financial reports, consumer payment-account fees, basic payment account, payment statistics, Centralni registar transakcionih racuna, prinudna naplata. Instant-payments and TIPS onboarding are live compliance-deadline generators for Montenegrin PSPs.

source_name: CBCG — Sanacija kreditnih institucija (resolution authority function)
why_relevant: CBCG acts as the national resolution authority: resolution objectives and instruments, the sanacioni fond and its contributions, and MREL requirements. MREL calibration and contribution calls are hard-dated obligations on every bank and a distinct regulatory workstream from prudential supervision.

source_name: CBCG — Nadzor u oblasti sprjecavanja pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (AML/CFT supervision)
why_relevant: AML/CFT supervisory channel including the CBCG's regulatory role, guidelines for risk analysis and for establishing ML/TF risk-management systems (e.g. Sl. list CG 55/24), and supervisory expectations for obliged entities. AML is Montenegro's most active EU-accession-driven compliance area and a frequent source of new obligations and deadlines.

source_name: CBCG — Zastita prava klijenata kreditnih institucija i korisnika finansijskih usluga
why_relevant: Conduct-supervision channel plus registers of credit intermediaries and housing-loan mediators; pairs with the 'zastita korisnika potrosackih kredita' bylaw category (effective interest rate, creditworthiness assessment, intermediary registration). Conduct rules bind directly on bank and PSP product operations.

source_name: CBCG — Finansijska stabilnost / makroprudencijalne mjere
why_relevant: Macroprudential policy channel: countercyclical capital buffer, systemic risk buffer, borrower-based measures on household lending, and payment-system oversight. Buffer decisions carry explicit forward application dates (e.g. CCyB 1% applicable 1 January 2026; borrower-based measures extended to 1 January 2026), which are exactly the deadline objects this workstream tracks.

source_name: CBCG — Publikacije / redovne publikacije (supervision and stability reporting)
why_relevant: Scheduled institutional reporting: Izvjestaj o radu CBCG, Izvjestaj guvernerke o sprovodjenju politike, Izvjestaj o stabilnosti finansijskog sistema, Makroprudencijalna analiza i politika, Bilten CBCG, macroeconomic reports and the bank credit-activity survey. These narrate supervisory priorities (e.g. SREP alignment with ECB methodology) and pre-announce forthcoming regulatory work.

source_name: CBCG — Politika CBCG i Strateski plan (annual policy and multi-year strategy)
why_relevant: The annual Politika CBCG and the Strateski plan CBCG 2025-2028 state, ex ante, which regulations the bank intends to draft in the coming period (EU-integration alignment, ECB SREP methodology adoption). Best single forward-looking indicator of the regulatory pipeline before any draft exists.

source_name: CBCG — Pristup informacijama / javni registri i javne evidencije (FOI channel)
why_relevant: Free-access-to-information channel with the Vodic za slobodan pristup informacijama and an enumerated inventory of the public registers and evidencije the CBCG holds. The inventory page is itself a pointer that reveals datasets not linked from the main navigation, and the FOI route is the legitimate escalation path for supervisory material that is not proactively published.

source_name: CBCG — Elektronski servisi (e-service portals)
why_relevant: Index of six CBCG digital service platforms (auctions, resident reporting, enforcement/prinudna naplata systems, transaction-account registry lookups). Each portal is a separate host/application whose terms of use and technical access model must be assessed independently before any collection.

source_name: Sluzbeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette of Montenegro)
why_relevant: The legally authoritative promulgation venue for every CBCG Odluka and every law the CBCG applies. The 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation stamped on each bylaw resolves here, giving the canonical text and the exact publication date from which stupanje na snagu and compliance deadlines are computed. Adjacent to the CBCG cell but indispensable to it.

source_name: eUprava Crne Gore — e-participacija / javne rasprave
why_relevant: Montenegro's statutory public-consultation portal. Critically, CBCG-drafted primary legislation is consulted here by the Ministarstvo finansija, not on cbcg.me: the Nacrt zakona o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kreditnim institucijama (crypto-asset scope, ownership-stake rules, management accountability, ESG in banking supervision) ran a 20-day consultation via the ministry site and eUprava. Consultation windows carry an explicit rok za dostavljanje komentara.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (gov.me) — financial-sector legislative pipeline
why_relevant: The ministry is the formal proposer of CBCG-drafted banking and payments statutes and runs their public consultations, publishes the nacrt text, the obrazlozenje and the post-consultation report. Confirmed in this run for the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama amendments and the Zakon o finansijskim konglomeratima amendments. Any CBCG regulatory watch that monitors only cbcg.me will miss the primary-law stage entirely.

source_name: Skupstina Crne Gore — zakoni.skupstina.me (parliamentary legislative tracker)
why_relevant: Terminal stage of the pipeline: predlog zakona texts, amendments, committee materials and adoption dates for banking and payments statutes. Gives the definitive adoption date from which CBCG must issue implementing Odluke, and typically the transposition/implementation deadlines written into the prelazne i zavrsne odredbe.

source_name: PropisiNet.me — consolidated Montenegrin legislation database
why_relevant: Commercial legal aggregator that publishes per-issue tables of contents of the Sluzbeni list and maintains consolidated ('preciscen') texts of laws such as the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama, plus a 'dnevna azurnost' daily-update feed. Extremely useful as a low-friction change detector for CBCG instruments and as a cross-check that no gazette issue was missed; not authoritative and largely subscription-gated for full text.

source_name: Katalog Propisa (katalogpropisa.me) — regulation update catalogue
why_relevant: Second commercial Montenegrin regulation catalogue exposing a 'pregled azuriranih propisa' (list of recently updated regulations). Serves as a redundant change-detection channel independent of PropisiNet, useful for catching amendments to CBCG bylaws quickly.

source_name: Investitor.me — Montenegrin financial trade press
why_relevant: Specialist Montenegrin finance/business outlet that covers CBCG regulatory moves substantively rather than as briefs — e.g. it reported the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama consultation and unpacked the crypto-asset scope, ownership-stake and ESG-supervision changes. Valuable for interpretation and for surfacing consultations whose primary announcement is easy to miss.

source_name: Kodex.me — Montenegrin business/legal news
why_relevant: Covers the closing phase of financial-sector consultations, including outcomes such as all comments being accepted on the Zakon o finansijskim konglomeratima amendments. Useful for the consultation-outcome stage that official portals report late or only as PDF annexes.

source_name: CBCG — LinkedIn company channel
why_relevant: First-party social amplification of CBCG announcements; occasionally posts consultation invitations and event notices ahead of, or instead of, a full website item. Low incremental value versus the saopstenja feed and hostile to automated collection.
